batadal.source: github.com/scy-phy/ICS-Evasion-Attacks at commit 56ce09031ed8d480fc2a34313009ba534e7c12ec, Data/BATADAL (the C-Town network re-simulated without concealment by Erba et al., ACSAC 2020); git blob sha1 verified
batadal.lineage_status: Never downloaded or used by any earlier FerrumOS study. The repository's real_telemetry_sources_v1.json cites the BATADAL paper only as a source of attack-family descriptions for synthetic injection design.
seen_so_far: The header line of all three CSV files (columns: DATETIME as elapsed hours, 19 PRESSURE, 12 FLOW and 12 STATUS columns, ATT_FLAG).

The whole training file, as development data: 48,106 rows over 384 days, regular 15-minute reports plus extra rows at control events, ATT_FLAG 0 on every row, FLOW_PU5, FLOW_PU9, STATUS_PU5 and STATUS_PU9 constant.

The repository file listing, which also holds 14 per-attack extracts (attack_1..14_from_test_dataset.csv) with their byte sizes (23 KB to 121 KB); the sizes indicate attack durations roughly. These extracts were not downloaded or read.
The README of the repository (no data description).
batadal.prior_knowledge_disclosure: The author knows the BATADAL competition design from Taormina et al. (2018): seven attacks in each of the two attack datasets, staged on tank levels, pump and valve controls, originally with concealment. The scy-phy version removes the concealment.
batadal.development_data: train_dataset.csv on a 15-minute grid: 36,856 steps (384 days), 31 sensors and 12 actions before dropping 4 constant columns.
